sm: A Catholic healthcare provider, Calvary Health Care, is set to take over fourteen private hospitals in Australia after the collapse of operator Healthscope. The competition regulator approved the deal on the twenty-fifth of November, finding Calvary the only realistic buyer. State and territory licensing approval is still needed. Under Calvary's ethical standards, elective abortion, assisted suicide, IVF and gender-affirming procedures will not be offered, though maternity, cancer, intensive care and rehabilitation services continue, and women whose lives are at risk will still be treated, including for ectopic pregnancies. Critics say public hospitals may face more pressure, and New South Wales will open theatres at a Newcastle public hospital for affected IVF patients. Peter Kearney of SPUC said Calvary's stance is consistent with its mission and deserves recognition.
